text:
olivia: quick follow-up from the scheduler breakout: idea is to pack microwindows by cost-quantile instead of raw token count. goal = reduce stragglers without blocking tiny cheap requests. reactions?
ryan: interesting. so essentially compute a cost_score per request, map to quantile q in [0..N), and only coalesce same q within a microwindow?
leah: yeah. pros: batches stay more homogeneous. cons: might hurt headroom utilization if many requests land in the same high-quantile bucket. we should simulate.
matt: micro-constraints: admission must still be sub-300us. computing quantile must be O(1). precompute model->quantile thresholds in shared mem. request hits: score -> binary search on small array or use clamp(math.floor(score / step)). cheap.
maya: observability: record assigned_quantile and actual_compute_units. we can auto-tune thresholds using drift detection. also add metric for cross-quantile contamination (how often a batch ends up with >1 quantile).
olivia: fallback for unseen prompts? proposal: bloom filter for known prompt-signatures that maps to cached score; if miss, use profile median for model+length. bloom avoids RPCs.
ryan: bloom false positives mean we might reuse wrong score occasionally. acceptable if we track residuals and decay entries on mismatch.
leah: how to handle fairness? a tenant blasting high-cost quantile could monopolize a GPU. suggest per-tenant soft-weights: each tenant has a credit bucket of compute_units. admission decrements estimated_cost, queue rejects or routes to fallback if below threshold. credits refill at tenant-rate.
matt: that ties into runtime: per-GPU leaky-bucket for global headroom + per-tenant soft-ledger. both in shared mem. need eviction policy when ledger inconsistent across hosts. periodic reconcile is fine.
olivia: deployment concerns: incremental rollout with canary -> flag to enable quantile bucketing. make default = off.
maya: dashboard plan: 1) quantile assignment distribution, 2) quantile vs actual cost heatmap, 3) per-tenant credit utilization. add alert for median residual > 30%.
metricsbot: :bar_chart: quantile_experiment_01 started for canary group runtime-canary-7. sampling rate 1% initial.
ryan: small simulation notes: if N too large we fragment batches; N too small we regain heterogeneity. sweet spot likely 4-8 quantiles per model class. include model-specific N.
leah: another wrinkle: decoder-state influence. same prompt length may diverge mid-generation if model caches differ. suggest admission only uses prefill cost (tokens before first gen). streaming tail handled by soft-evict if runtime exceeds budget.
matt: soft-evict design sketch: mark a batch as \"overflowing\" and either slice trailing generation (emit partial) or move trailing slots to emergency fastpath if available. must be transparent to caller (status codes + partial output).
olivia: API impact: no change to public API. enqueue proto gets internal-only hint fields: cost_score, quantile_hint, tenant_credit_hint. all optional.
ryan: unit tests: fake profiles with bimodal costs and assert batching reduces 99th percentile latency vs token-only packing. I'll own the sim.
maya: telemetry spike: instrument estimated_vs_actual per request and expose rolling kde for each model-version. also tag events where tenant_credit < 0 (rejects).
leah: can we avoid blocking low-cost requests behind bucket fill? proposal: prioritize low-quantile buckets for fill-timeouts; if low-quantile batch hasn't filled after T_hold small, flush. pick T_hold per quantile (smaller for low-cost).
olivia: action items: ryan -> sim + suggested N per model class; leah -> soft-evict small design doc + hold-time sketch; matt -> shared-mem layout & reconcile protocol; maya -> telemetry + dashboard mockups; I'll wire the feature flag and bake canary. reconvene EOD with bench numbers.
ryan: noted, starting sim now. will post a short csv of throughput vs p99 for different N.
maya: I'll add the metric names to the infra catalog: runtime.quantile_assigned, runtime.estimated_compute, runtime.actual_compute, runtime.residual_pct, runtime.tenant_credit_balance.
olivia: sweet. keep the canary small and watch quota drains. then plan for 2-phase: quantile-only (no tenant credits) -> enable soft-credits if safe.
metricsbot: :white_check_mark: canary sampling bumped to 5% for runtime-canary-7 per request.
leah: one tiny UX ask: when soft-evict slices output, include metadata \"evicted_by\": \"soft-evict\" and \"eviction_reason\": \"compute_budget_exceeded\" so customers can surface this.
matt: agreed. also track evicted_units counter per model so ops can tune per-model profiles.
olivia: great thread. will follow up with a tiny RFC blurb and link to the sim results. meeting next Tue to decide roll-forward. :rocket:
